steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease an 11x7 inch baking dish.

Place bacon in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium high heat until evenly brown. Drain, crumble and set aside. While bacon is cooking, wash tomatoes and slice off stem ends. Gently scoop out pulp, leaving a 1/2 inch wall. Finely chop pulp and place 1/3 cup of it in a medium bowl. You may discard remaining pulp.

Stir crumbled bacon, green pepper, cheese, croutons, and salt and pepper into tomato pulp. Spoon an equal amount of mixture into each hollowed out tomato. Place stuffed tomatoes into prepared baking dish.
Bake in preheated oven for 20 to 25 minutes, until heated through. Garnish with parsley sprigs.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Stuffed Tomatoes
raw_recipe.description: An easy and quick recipe for when tomatoes are abundant from your garden.

review.reviewBody: I've made these several times for Jason and myself as a light lunch or dinner. I've made them by Anita's original recipe, and I've also made the following changes: I've added shredded swiss cheese and chopped onions and red and yellow peppers as well as green. I've added a chopped, seeded jalapeno pepper to the mix. I've substituted cubed cooked ham and also cubes of kielbasa instead of bacon. And I've replaced the Parmesan with Ricotta for a richer filling. I'm convinced that there is no way to mess this recipe up-it turns out perfect every time. Thanks Anita-your recipe is great as is, but serves VERY well as a foundation for changes!

I made lots of changes. We're vegetarian, so no bacon. Used feta instead of parmesan. Diced and sauteed: 1/4 onion, 1/3 red pepper, 1 yellow squash. Added to all of the tomato pulp (diced and lightly drained). Used fresh basil instead of what the recipe called for. Oh, and breadcrumbs instead of croutons. Really good!
...I used small(ish) eggplant instead of tomatoes (I ran out of tomatoes!), and used panko & bacon, also used Gruyere (it's what I had!) & smoked salmon...It was yummy!

This turned out amazing! So flavourful and delicious (and I don't even like tomatoes raw) I used garlic and herb feta cheese, and I added onions with the green peppers which I sauteed in the bacon fat before adding it to the stuffing mixture. Went great with steak and salad. Enjoy!!

This was OK, but not great. I think the stuffing needs more flavour - onion, garlic, that kind of taste. I also didn't like the green pepper still being crunchy after the tomatoes were done. I would saute it with the onion and garlic. It was nice, though to have a stuffed tomato without rice for a change.

One of the most succesful recipes I have tried off of allrecipes; my brother and I really enjoyed this

After reading the comments from a few reviewers, I upped the ingredients to avoid running out of stuffing, of course I ended up with too much, but the mixture is so flavorful (the bacon really sets it off) that it can be combined with lettuced for a great salad or mixed in with other vegetables

I used both shredded and canned parmesan cheese; I also mixed together bread crumbs and canned parmesan and sprinkled the mixture on the tops before baking.

Others mentioned that the green pepper didnt work for them; it worked fine for me so I think its a matter of taste. This is definitely a keeper for me

I did make changes to this, before adding the filling I smeared the inside of the tomatoes with sun dried tomato paste. I used a yellow bell pepper and chopped the parsley into the mix if I'd used it as a garnish hubby would have just put it on the side of his plate. I also made the croutons. Served with a rice salad this made a nice light evening meal. Thanks

I make spinach stuffed tomatoes occasionally, it's a side dish favorite. I made this for my wife last night. I left out the bell pepper, she don't care for that. But the bacon was a hit! Plus, I mixed in some shredded cheddar, and covered the tomato with a slice of provolone about 3 minutes before taking it out of the oven. She gave it 5 stars.
These were amazing!!! I added onions to them and a lot more cheese. I think maybe I'll try feta after the baby, but for now these are a wonderful addition to our meals.

This was delicious, I can't believe my husband actually liked it! I cut the bacon by half and replaced it with cooked ground hamburger and I also mixed in all of the pulp instead of discarding it to make it jucier!! Terrific recipe!

This was a great dish the only thing I did diffrently was omit the croutons as I was out. (still great without them though) and I added some garlic feta cheese. This is defintely a keeper. Thanks for sharing

I made this as a side dish to accompany crab cakes and corn on the cob. I did not make any changes except instead of croutons, I used Italian herb seasoned panko bread crumbs. It was a huge hit with fresh red tomatoes in season. Will make again and many requests for recipe by dinner guests!

I used brown rice because that was all I had, and we try to eat brown rice more than white. The taste was great, but the tomatoes collapsed...maybe they were too ripe. So, they didn't look great, but tasted nice...even my youngest son who is often hesitant to try new things liked it!
Used seasoned breadcrumbs instead of croutons and added a few drops of hot pepper oil. A great recipe I'll use often. Thanks
Tried it today. My difference was I exchanged bell peppers for cooked egg plant. It was heavenly
My picky husband said "The tomatoes are great!" at least three times during dinner. Afterwards he said "I definitely want those again!". Enough said! Great recipe! Thanks!
I added ground cooked sausage! Excellent!

I didn't use the bell pepper or parsley, simply because I forgot about the parsley and dislike bell peppers with a passion, but it turned out pretty good regardless. The croutons mashed up really made an awesome filler with the bacon & leftover tomato. Simple. Fun to make. And very enjoyable to eat.

Made these tonight & they were wonderful!! The recipe is perfect as is and is also a great jumping off place if you want to change it up. We had hollow tomatoes from the garden, so I did have to sacrifice the pulp from a regular tomatoe for the recipe.

Not bad. Quick to throw together, cute presentation. Next time I add this to a meal I'll tailor the spices and cheese to the main dish. The framework in this recipe holds together well for many different tastes.
